comparator.name: Artificial Intelligence
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official UvA study-programme page publishes a complete 180-EC curriculum: twelve named first-year components totalling 60 EC; twelve named second-year components totalling 60 EC; and a third year with 30 EC of electives, 6 EC of philosophy and ethics, 6 EC of Robots that Learn and an 18-EC graduation project. The official overview confirms the programme’s integration of computing, cognitive science, mathematical foundations, language and speech technology, machine learning and intelligent behaviour. The 30-EC elective space is preserved as a bounded curriculum component without inventing course titles.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match is complemented by two generator-backed and feasible organising directions: computational AI and autonomous intelligent systems; and cognitive AI, language and neuroscience. Each produces material curricular consequences and exceeds the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both provide a foundational introduction to programming for later computational study.
Both develop systematic software design and implementation practices.
Advanced Algorithms develops systematic computational problem solving; it is more algorithmically specialised than the UvA course.
Both directly cover data structures, algorithms and computational complexity.
Both use mathematical optimisation methods for computational and AI problems.
Both provide a dedicated introduction to machine-learning methods and model evaluation.
Both provide substantial neural-network theory and implementation, with UCR also extending into deep learning.
Both provide dedicated robotics study; UCR focuses on kinematics, manipulation and motion planning, while UvA emphasises learning robots.
Both directly cover image processing and computer-vision methods.
Both develop linear-algebra foundations through matrices, vectors and transformations.
Both develop formal logic and discrete reasoning for computing and AI.
Both combine probability and statistical inference for data-driven modelling.
Both develop mathematical methods for algorithms; UCR emphasises computational and numerical techniques.
Both investigate language processing; UCR focuses on human psycholinguistics rather than computational NLP.
Both provide philosophical analysis of mind and intelligence; UCR does not reproduce the full dedicated ethics component.
Both critically examine safety, fairness, responsibility, regulation and societal consequences of AI.
Both provide explicit first-year academic and professional formation; UCR PPD is broader than the AI-specific practicum.

notes.text: The UvA Artificial Intelligence bachelor provides a tightly integrated 180-EC sequence across programming, mathematics, statistics, machine learning, neural networks, cognitive modelling, natural-language processing, computer vision, logic, robotics, ethics, projects and an 18-EC graduation project. UCR can assemble strong interdisciplinary AI pathways with substantial programming, algorithms, data, machine learning, robotics, cognition, ethics and research, but it does not reproduce the same continuous specialist sequence or dedicated components in MLOps, probabilistic graphical models and computational NLP.
